Coram:
 Hon'Ble Mr. Justice Anish Dayal
 Order

These petitions have been filed for quashing of FIR No. 49/2019 registered at Sunlight Colony under Sections 498A/406/34 IPC on the ground that the parties have resolved their disputes in a settlement which forms part of divorce petition for mutual consent dated 11 th November, 2019 on the basis of which the decree was granted on 07 th December, 2019.
The petitioner No. 1 and respondent No. 2 had got married on 18th April, 2018 but due to mutual differences and disputes the marriage ended in a divorce.
The terms of the settlement, as per the counsels of the parties, have been carried out and no further payment is due.
Petitioner No. 1 and respondent No. 2 appear through VC and identified by the learned counsels and the Investigating Officer.
2. Considering the above settlement between the parties and chances of conviction of the petitioners being remote and bleak, there is no use to continue with proceedings of the present FIR.
Accordingly, the petition is allowed.
Consequently, the FIR No. 49/2019 under Sections 498A/406/34 IPC registered at PS Sunlight Colony and proceedings emanating therefrom are quashed.
3. Parties shall abide by the terms of settlement.
4. Accordingly, the petitions are disposed of.
Pending applications (if any) are disposed of as infructuous.

1. This appeal has been filed against the order 21 st May, 2019 passed by the learned ASJ in connection with Criminal Miscellaneous No. 11/2019 whereby the application preferred by the respondent (complainant) under Section 340 Cr.P.C. was allowed.
Now it transpires that cognizance has been taken on the said application and proceedings are pending before the learned Trial Court.

2. In view of no objection recorded in the settlement at para 7 (D), regarding the Section 340 Cr.P.C.
proceedings, by the respondent complainant, it would be appropriate if the appellant joins the proceedings and put on record this no objection given by the complainant.
3. In these circumstances, the application would then be decided by the learned Trial Court in accordance with law.
4. The Criminal Appeal therefore stands withdrawn at this stage with liberty to file afresh if need arises.
5. Accordingly, the appeal is disposed of.
6. Order be uploaded on the website of this Court.
